title: LVM
subtitle: Physical → volume group → logical volumes — flip for meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Logical Volume Manager — sits between physical disks and the file systems you mount
cards.notes: Pool disks and slice logical volumes you can resize instead of fixed partitions that are painful to grow.

cards.meaning: Physical disks/partitions → PV (pvcreate) → VG (vgcreate) → LV (lvcreate) → filesystem (mkfs + mount)
cards.notes: Memory hook: Physical → Volume group → Logical — initialize, pool, slice.

cards.meaning: A disk or partition labeled for LVM use
cards.notes: Initialized with pvcreate; shown with pvdisplay / pvscan.

cards.meaning: One pool of space made from one or more PVs
cards.notes: Any number of disks as one big disk.

cards.meaning: A slice of space carved from a VG — the block device you format and mount
cards.notes: Can span several disks; can be resized dynamically.

cards.meaning: Use any number of disks as one big disk; an LV can stretch across several disks
cards.notes: More flexible than raw partitions.

cards.meaning: Create small LVs and resize them dynamically; order on disk does not matter
cards.example: grow an LV without free space sitting next to it
cards.notes: You do not need free space adjacent to the LV inside the VG.

cards.meaning: Resize / create / delete logical and physical volumes online
cards.example: grow PV/LV while the system runs
cards.notes: The filesystem on the LV still needs its own resize; some filesystems support online resize.

cards.meaning: Move an LV that services are using to different disks without restarting those services
cards.example: live migrate LV to other disks
cards.notes: Services keep running during the move.

cards.meaning: Freeze a copy of the filesystem for backup with little downtime
cards.notes: Point-in-time copy for backup.

cards.meaning: Almost Linux-only — no official support on most other OS (FreeBSD, Windows, …)
cards.example: not portable to Windows as official LVM
cards.notes: Also more setup than plain partitions.

cards.meaning: Btrfs subvolumes already give a flexible layout — LVM on top may be unnecessary extra abstraction
cards.notes: Know when not to stack both.

cards.front: Create an LV in three steps
cards.meaning: 1) pvcreate 2) vgcreate 3) lvcreate — then mkfs and mount
cards.notes: Formatting is separate from LVM.

cards.meaning: Label a disk/partition as an LVM physical volume
cards.notes: “Physical volume successfully created.”

cards.meaning: Quick list of PVs: which exist, which VG they are in, how much is free
cards.notes: Example output shows Total / in use / in no VG.

cards.meaning: Detailed physical volume info
cards.notes: Shows fields like PV Name and VG Name.

cards.meaning: Create a volume group from one or more PVs
cards.notes: One PV or several PVs pooled into one VG.

cards.meaning: Detailed volume group info
cards.notes: Pair with vgscan to discover volume groups.

cards.meaning: Discover volume groups
cards.notes: Show/scan counterpart to vgcreate.

cards.meaning: Create a logical volume inside a volume group
cards.notes: LV lives inside a VG; then format with mkfs.

cards.meaning: Set the logical volume name
cards.notes: --name and -n are the same idea.

cards.meaning: Size the LV in bytes (G, M, …)
cards.notes: Fixed size, e.g. 2G.

cards.meaning: Size in logical extents — here, all remaining unallocated space in the VG
cards.notes: -l uses extents; -L uses byte sizes.

cards.meaning: List logical volumes — path, name, VG, status, size
cards.notes: Example fields: LV Path, LV Name, VG Name, LV Status available, LV Size.

cards.meaning: Short scan of logical volumes
cards.notes: Show/scan counterpart to lvcreate.

cards.meaning: Typically /dev/<vg_name>/<lv_name> and also /dev/mapper/<vg_name>-<lv_name>
cards.notes: Also /dev/mapper/vg_newlvm-centos7_newvol.

cards.meaning: Format a filesystem on the LV — LVM only gives you a block device
cards.notes: Also mkfs.btrfs, mkfs.ntfs in the notes. Then mount; add /etc/fstab to survive reboot.

cards.meaning: Mount the filesystem on the LV so you can use it
cards.notes: Persist with /etc/fstab if needed.

cards.meaning: df -h = space; lsblk = which LV sits on which disk; findmnt = mount table
cards.notes: Filesystem layer tools after mkfs + mount.
